title: Digital transformation OF higher education: continuity or disruption, utopia or dystopia

scope.of_vs_in: The inquiry concerns the digital transformation OF higher education (what HE is: its form, functions, boundaries, legitimacy and mandate), not digitalization IN higher education (tools used inside existing structures and their effectiveness for learning outcomes).
scope.doctoral_training: Doctoral training is a separate line of inquiry and is out of scope here; the doctoral level enters only as one level of the degree structure when the evidence addresses it.
scope.no_stage_models: No linear development-stage framing. Variation across regions is treated as historical and contextual diversity; sources that use stage or catch-up models are reported together with the critiques of those models.
scope.analogy_not_forecast: Historical and scenario material is an analogy base and a map of arguments, not a forecast. No 5/10/15/20-year projections are made in this package.

guiding_questions: What is the status of research on the digital transformation of higher education?
What might HE look like in 5, 10, 15 and 20 years? (not answered in this package; see scope)
Will we still reason in terms of BSc, MSc and doctoral studies, HEIs as the places where R&D&I happens, and HEIs as agents of change?
With so much automated reasoning, what will universities look like and what will their role be?

axes.label: Continuity versus disruption
axes.question: Does the underlying logic of the role, practice, institution or mandate persist, or is it displaced?
axes.note: Milestones also use layered (addition and recombination with persistence) and mixed. Continuity and disruption are independent of utopian or dystopian valence.

axes.label: Utopian versus dystopian
axes.question: Is the outcome beneficial or harmful, and for whom?
axes.note: Always read together with the "for whom". The same development is read as utopian by some authors and dystopian by others.

cross_level_tension: A cross-level tension is a development that is positive at one level and negative at another (for example productivity gains for individual researchers coinciding with narrowing of collective research focus).

rate_of_change.principle: Layered, not a single curve. No composite index.
